title: Hunts FH-042S: Player answer form and authoring for choices and Mystery

source.ref: Split from FH-042 (2026-11-16): the branch engine, the server-only answer check and the claim path shipped dark; the screens and authoring move here.

detail:
Requires FH-042, FH-030S. The engine and the claim door accept choices and Mystery answers, but no screen reaches them. Build: (1) the player answer form on the play and scan screens, passing the answer to claimAsPlayer and wording answer_required, answer_wrong (attempts left, the hint), answer_locked (point at the fallback stop) and a closed branch, per docs/NAMING.md and docs/CONTENT-VOICE.md; (2) the projection for a locked-out Mystery, so projectForPlayer stops naming it as the next stop once its attempts are used; (3) authoring through a lib/studio entity: choice_group, fallback_group, mission kind answer, and the answer itself written only through hashAnswer (lib/hunts/mystery.ts) so the plain answer is never stored, with validateGraph blockers shown before publish; (4) a decision, recorded as an ADR if taken, on whether hunt_claim_apply should itself refuse a second member of a choice group, which would close the staff-approval gap named in FH-042 and needs a migration through the serial database gate; (5) a pgTAP or live two-session run of two branches claimed at once against real Postgres, which the FH-042 tests only model. Done when: a player can answer a Mystery on a phone, a wrong and a locked answer read clearly, a creator can publish a fork and a Mystery without touching JSON, and the two-session race is recorded against the real database. Owner role: Game systems. Hunts switches stay OFF.

Built 2026-11-16, dark. Player: the Trail page and the scan screen take a Mystery answer through one form (components/hunts/claim-stop-form.tsx) and pass it to claimAsPlayer; app/(main)/hunts/[slug]/play/actions.ts words answer_required, answer_wrong (tries left, and the stop's hint from the second wrong try), answer_locked (naming the stand-in stop from the Mystery's fallback group) and a stop closed by the other path at a fork (lib/hunts/player.ts answerRefusalWords, standInPositions). The scan POST (app/(main)/hunts/p/[code]/route.ts) accepts one optional answer field, keeps it out of the landing URL, and hands an unanswered Mystery to the same form with the scanned code. Projection: lib/hunts/claim-store.ts loadLockedAnswers reads the run's answer:<n> rows (lockedMysteries in lib/hunts/mystery.ts) and projectForPlayer closes a Mystery with no tries left, so the stand-in becomes the next stop; closed stops say why (other path, not needed, no tries left). Authoring: the Hunt Studio entity (lib/studio/entities/hunt.ts) gains Forks (stops a player picks one of, published as choice_group choice-N) and Mystery stops (stop, a write-only answer, a stand-in stop, published as kind answer with a shared fallback_group mystery-N), kept as separate repeats keyed by stop so the pinned stop field list is unchanged. lib/hunts/draft.ts derives the graph (a fork or a Mystery and its stand-in share a Trail step; the next step opens on any of them), publishes answer_hash, and words BRANCH_INVALID, CHOICE_LIMIT, BRANCH_DEAD_END and MYSTERY_NO_FALLBACK for the resident, plus a mystery_answer checklist item. The save action seals a typed answer with hashAnswer before the draft is read (sealDraftAnswers), and parseTrailDraft keeps only a well-formed hash, so the plain answer is never stored. No migration. Items (4), the SQL refusal of a second choice-group member in hunt_claim_apply, and (5), the two-session race against real Postgres, need a migration through the serial gate and a live database: split to FH-042T. Hunts switches stay off.
